instructions: A pointer stores the memory address of another variable. Use * to declare.
task: Create int x = 10. Create pointer 'ptr' pointing to x. Print x using ptr.
hint: Use & to get address, * to dereference pointer.
title: Basic Pointer

instructions: Use & to get the address of a variable.
task: Create int num = 42. Print its address (use &num).
hint: Use & to get the memory address: cout << #
title: Address Of

instructions: Pointers can change the value they point to.
task: Create int x = 5. Pointer ptr = &x. Change *ptr to 20. Print x.
hint: *ptr = 20; changes the value at that address.
title: Change via Pointer

instructions: Null pointers point to nothing. Use nullptr.
task: Create int* ptr = nullptr. Check if ptr is null and print 'Null'.
hint: if (ptr == nullptr) cout << "Null";
title: Null Pointer

instructions: Pointers can be reassigned to different variables.
task: Create int a = 1, b = 2. Pointer ptr = &a. Change ptr to &b. Print *ptr.
hint: ptr = &b; changes the pointer to point to b.
title: Reassign Pointer

instructions: Pointer arithmetic moves the pointer by size of type.
task: Create int arr[3] = {10, 20, 30}. Pointer ptr = arr. Print *(ptr + 1).
hint: ptr + 1 points to the next element.
title: Pointer Arithmetic

instructions: Pointers can be compared using == or !=.
task: Create int x = 5. Two pointers p1 = &x, p2 = &x. Check if equal and print 'Same'.
hint: if (p1 == p2) cout << "Same";
title: Compare Pointers

instructions: Pass pointers to functions to modify values.
task: Create function 'increment(int* p)' that adds 1 to *p. Call with x = 5. Print x.
hint: Use *p += 1 inside function.
title: Pointer to Function

instructions: Dynamic memory uses new and delete.
task: Create int* p = new int(10). Print *p, then delete p.
hint: int* p = new int(10); ... delete p;
title: Dynamic Memory

instructions: Pointer to pointer stores address of another pointer.
task: Create int x = 5. Pointer p = &x. Pointer pp = &p. Print **pp.
hint: int** pp = &p; — double pointer.
title: Pointer to Pointer

instructions: An array stores multiple values of the same type.
task: Create int array {10, 20, 30} and print the first element.
title: Create Array

instructions: Loop through array using index.
task: Create array {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. Print each element on a new line.
hint: for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) cout << arr[i] << endl;
title: Loop Array

instructions: Calculate sum of all array elements.
task: Create array {10, 20, 30}. Print the sum.
hint: Use a loop to add each element.
title: Array Sum

instructions: Find the maximum value in an array.
task: Create array {5, 15, 8}. Find and print the largest.
hint: Start with arr[0] and compare each element.
title: Array Max

instructions: Reverse an array by swapping elements.
task: Create array {1, 2, 3}. Print in reverse order.
hint: Loop from end to start: for (int i = 2; i >= 0; i--)
title: Reverse Array

instructions: Count how many elements are even.
task: Create array {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}. Print count of even numbers.
hint: Use if (arr[i] % 2 == 0) count++;
title: Count Even

instructions: 2D arrays are arrays of arrays.
task: Create 2D array {{1, 2}, {3, 4}}. Print the element at [1][0].
title: 2D Array

instructions: Copy array elements to another array.
task: Create arr1 = {1, 2, 3}. Copy to arr2. Print arr2[2].
hint: for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) arr2[i] = arr1[i];
title: Copy Array

instructions: Search for a value in an array.
task: Create array {10, 20, 30}. Search for 20. Print 'Found' if exists.
hint: Loop and check if arr[i] == 20.
title: Search Array

instructions: Sort array using std::sort.
task: Create array {3, 1, 2}. Sort and print all elements.
hint: Use sort(arr, arr + 3); then print each.
title: Sort Array

instructions: Inheritance allows a class to inherit properties from another class.
task: Create base class 'Animal' with method 'sound()' printing 'Generic'. Create 'Dog' inheriting Animal. Call d.sound().
hint: class Dog : public Animal { };
title: Basic Inheritance

instructions: Derived class can override base class method.
task: Create Animal with sound() 'Generic'. Dog overrides sound() to 'Woof'. Call Dog's sound().
hint: Redefine sound() inside Dog class.
title: Method Override

instructions: Use 'protected' for members accessible by derived classes.
task: Create Animal with protected 'name'. Dog sets name to 'Buddy' in constructor. Print it.
hint: Use 'protected: string name;' — accessible to derived.
title: Protected Member

instructions: Constructor of base class runs before derived class constructor.
task: Animal constructor prints 'Animal', Dog constructor prints 'Dog'. Create Dog and see order.
hint: Base constructor runs first, then derived.
title: Constructor Order

instructions: Multiple inheritance: class inherits from 2 classes.
task: Create classes 'A' with method a(), 'B' with b(). Class 'C' inherits both. Call c.a() and c.b().
hint: class C : public A, public B { };
title: Multiple Inheritance

instructions: virtual functions allow polymorphism.
task: Create Animal with virtual sound() 'Generic'. Dog overrides to 'Woof'. Use Animal pointer, call sound().
hint: Mark base method as virtual for runtime polymorphism.
title: Virtual Function

instructions: Abstract class has pure virtual function.
task: Create abstract 'Shape' with pure virtual area(). Implement 'Square' with area() returning side*side. Print Square(5).area().
hint: virtual double area() = 0; — pure virtual.
title: Abstract Class

instructions: Call parent method using ClassName::method().
task: Animal has sound() 'Generic'. Dog overrides but calls Animal::sound() first, then 'Woof'. Print both.
hint: Call parent: Animal::sound();
title: Call Parent Method

instructions: Multi-level inheritance: A → B → C.
task: A has method a(), B inherits A, C inherits B. Create C and call a().
hint: class B : public A { }; class C : public B { };
title: Multi-level Inherit

instructions: Polymorphism: different classes behave differently via base pointer.
task: Abstract Animal with virtual speak(). Cat returns 'Meow', Dog returns 'Woof'. Loop array of Animal* and call speak().
hint: Base class virtual method — each derived overrides.
title: Polymorphism
